name: Light Burgundy
lede: Light Burgundy is a muted purplish red built by adding the modifier "light" to [[burgundy]], first recorded in the 2010 xkcd color survey rather than in any older color dictionary.

sections.title: A modifier on Burgundy
sections.body:
Light Burgundy follows ordinary English modifier grammar: "light" attached to the wine-named color [[burgundy]] [1]. Our library's earliest record of the exact name comes from the xkcd color survey, a 2010 crowdsourced naming project, not from Ridgway's 1912 atlas or the 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary, neither of which lists this precise tint by name [1].

In our color library its nearest neighbor is [[light-maroon]], about 2.9 units away and duller, followed by Pomegranate Purple at 3.2 units, almost indistinguishable on screen [2]. [[dark-rose]] sits 3.8 units off, also close, while [[solferino]] and Maroon X11 are duller and more vivid respectively [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive of 23,781 paintings matches this tone in only 18 of them, about 0.08 percent, as photographed, rarer than 68 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, present in 5 of the 1,674 paintings from that decade, 4.2 times the rate its museums' own baseline would predict [3].

Inside a painting it most often plays an accent across its 10 clearly-ranked appearances [3]. The earliest dated match in our archive is 1609, in a painting by El Greco [3]. The archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first. That is 401 years before the name's first record, in the 2010 xkcd survey, so the match is a look-alike hue in an old photograph, not proof the name existed then [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and the match is a computed color reading, not a pigment identification [3].
